subject: Re: Audit rights, pen-test window & escrow clause - coordination
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@atlashealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@atlashealth.com
Date: 2027-05-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Audit rights + pen-test coordination for order form

Mina —

Thanks for the draft order form and the security exhibit. Legal has a couple of asks before we can sign: the audit rights clause needs clarification on the notice window and the scope of forensic access during SOC 2 inspections; additionally our infra/security team needs a firm pen-test window and list of required artifact owners.

Can you confirm:
- The minimum notice Redwood requires before an on-site or remote inspection (we typically request 10 business days)
- Whether your pen-test access will include ephemeral log exports or only scoped remote access to test hosts
- A single ops contact and an escalation contact from Redwood for the test day

We've attached our internal checklist — hoping to align this week so procurement can clear the PO.

Thanks,
Samir Patel
Director, InfoSec — AtlasHealth
attachments: Atlas_Checklist_Reqs.xlsx
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@atlashealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-04T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Audit rights + pen-test coordination for order form

Samir —

Appreciate the checklist. Quick answers up front:
- Notice window: we can do 10 business days for on-site inspections; for remote SOC 2 evidence requests we typically ask 5 business days. We can make the order form language say "reasonable notice (no less than 5 business days); on-site inspections require 10 business days" if that helps.
- Pen-test access: Redwood allows scoped remote testing only (no on-host persistence or human-initiated data exfil). We can provide ephemeral log exports and scoped network access for the authorized IP range during the agreed window — we'll capture artifacts needed for your review.
- Contacts: ops on the day will be Aditya Rao (aditya_rao@redwood.ai) and escalation to Karthik Iyer on legal/contract exceptions.

I attached an updated security exhibit (v1.4) and a proposed pen-test scope spreadsheet showing the authorized hosts and timing windows. Laura and Karthik — added you for redlines on the audit-rights paragraph and the proposed escrow/backstop language.

Next steps: if you and procurement are good with the 5/10 business day split and the scoped remote-only pen test, we can push the updated order form today and ask for a targeted sign-off by EOD Friday (5/7).

Best,
Mina Haddad
Head of Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference
attachments: Redwood_Security_Exhibit_v1.4.pdf, pen-test-scope-atlashealth.xlsx
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Samir Patel <samir@atlashealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-05T09:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Audit rights + pen-test coordination for order form 

Samir / Mina —

Thanks for the proposed language. A few legal redlines and clarifications from our side to avoid ambiguity:

1) Audit window / scope: replace the open-ended "reasonable notice" phrasing with: "Customer may request audit access no more than once per 12-month period, with notice no less than 10 business days for on-site inspections and no less than 5 business days for remote evidence requests. Access will be limited to records and systems necessary to validate Redwood's SOC 2 Controls as set forth in the Security Exhibit." This prevents frequent ad-hoc requests.

2) Pen-test constraints: add explicit prohibition on persistence, privilege escalation attempts that could impact multi-tenant hosts, and a requirement that any exploit artifacts be shared only as sanitized summaries. We will provide ephemeral logs and a read-only bucket for artifact exports.

3) Escrow/backstop: because you asked about escrow earlier, propose the following limited backstop: "In the extremely limited event of prolonged inability to access services for more than 72 continuous hours due to Redwood operational failure confirmed by both parties, Redwood will make available a transitional data export under an agreed NDPA. This is not a general escrow of source." This is intentionally narrow — pls confirm if Atlas needs broader.

4) Evidence cadence: propose a quarterly evidence bundle for SOC 2-adjacent customers (SOC 2 reports + attestation doc + audit logs for the prior 90 days) and ad-hoc additional exports on request subject to the notice windows above and a mutually agreed bandwidth cap.

Mina — happy to drop these into the redline for the order form. Samir — please flag any of the above must-haves from Atlas and I'll iterate.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Samir Patel <samir@atlashealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Audit rights + pen-test coordination for order form

Karthik / Mina —

Thanks, that language looks sensible and addresses most of our concerns. A couple of small follow-ups from our infra team:

- Can you confirm the exact SLAs around artifact delivery (we typically request logs within 48 hours of receipts) — Karthik's quarterly bundle + ad-hoc sounds fine but we need confirmation on delivery timing for ad-hoc exports.
- For the pen-test day please list the start/end UTC times and the exact contact phone number for Aditya (we will add to our runbook).

If you can add the 48-hour artifact delivery SLA to the evidence cadence paragraph and confirm Aditya's phone, procurement will clear the PO and we can sign the order form.

I'll mark this green pending those two items.

Samir Patel
Director, InfoSec — AtlasHealth
